# nature::model and nature::errorbar

<!-- Generated by scripts/check_spec.py from docs/spec/nature-physical-model.toml. Edit that file and run `python3 scripts/check_spec.py --write`. -->

The properties of the physical models of historical Stage 6, from ADR 0002 §4 and §5. A model on a smooth affine object X names a symmetric endomorphism field H of `std::linalg::spectral`, a reading of X, the convention `hbar_one`, a prepared and an observed basis vector of the module of H, the transition average that it predicts and its regime. A calibration gives measured values, an exact value with a standard uncertainty each, to coordinates of X. A dataset of a model under a calibration has a coverage factor k and points that give the other coordinates and a measured value of the observable. A comparison records a dataset, the fingerprint of its calibration and a verdict. The modules declare the families `Model<X>`, `Calibration<X>`, `Dataset<X>` and `Comparison<X>`; the application declares its conventions, models, calibrations, datasets and comparisons.

[Specifications](../specifications.md) defines the [claim statuses](../specifications.md#claim-statuses) and the checks. This chapter is generated from [`docs/spec/nature-physical-model.toml`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/docs/spec/nature-physical-model.toml).

<a id="physical-model.references"></a>

## A model names a field, a reading and an average that fit

- Property: `physical-model.references`
- Subject: `nature::model::Model`
- Rule: [ADR 0002 §4, Contract and jurisdiction](../adr/0002-nature-dimension.md#contract-and-jurisdiction-1)

An accepted model's reading is a reading of the object of the model, its prepared and observed vectors are basis vectors of the free module of its hamiltonian, and the average that it predicts is a transition average of a branch of that hamiltonian from the prepared to the observed vector. Any other model is an error (`E_MODEL`). The convention of a model is `hbar_one`.

- Example: In the two-level program, the model of H = (Δ/2)σ_z + (Ω/2)σ_x prepared in g and observed in e predicts the average A from g to e. A prepared vector f1 of another free module W of the same chart is an error (`E_MODEL`), and so is a reading of another chart Q with the same coordinates.
- Run by: `book_rejected_packages_print_their_diagnostics` in [`tests/examples.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/examples.rs)

Claims:

- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `book_rejected_packages_print_their_diagnostics` in [`tests/examples.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/examples.rs)
    - `forged_stage6_records_are_rejected_by_the_kernel` in [`tests/physical_models.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/physical_models.rs)
    - [`VastitasKernel.NatureModelRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasKernel/NatureModelRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)
    - [`VastitasKernel.ModelDeclarationRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasKernel/ModelDeclarationRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)
  - Note: The rejected packages `two-level-other-basis` and `two-level-other-reading` give the two `E_MODEL` diagnostics of the example. The forged wire prepares the observed vector, which the kernel rejects with `E_MODEL`.
- `oracle`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#841](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/841)

<a id="physical-model.chart"></a>

## Every data point lies on the chart of the prediction

- Property: `physical-model.chart`
- Subject: `nature::errorbar::Dataset`
- Rule: [ADR 0002 §5, Contract and jurisdiction](../adr/0002-nature-dimension.md#contract-and-jurisdiction-2)

With the calibrated values, every point of an accepted dataset lies on the chart D(g) of the branch of the average that its model predicts, whatever the closed form of the average. A point off the chart is an error (`E_ERRORBAR`). An accepted dataset has at least one point, and each point gives exactly the coordinates that its calibration does not give.

- Example: With the detuning calibrated at Δ = 0, a point with the Rabi frequency Ω = 0 lies where the two eigenvalues of H meet, off D(Δ² + Ω²), and is an error (`E_ERRORBAR`).
- Run by: `book_rejected_packages_print_their_diagnostics` in [`tests/examples.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/examples.rs)

Claims:

- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `book_rejected_packages_print_their_diagnostics` in [`tests/examples.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/examples.rs)
    - [`VastitasKernel.NatureModelRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasKernel/NatureModelRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)
  - Note: The rejected package `two-level-off-chart` gives the diagnostic of the example.

<a id="physical-model.verdict"></a>

## The verdict is recomputed exactly

- Property: `physical-model.verdict`
- Subject: `nature::errorbar::Comparison`
- Rule: [ADR 0002 §5, Contract and jurisdiction](../adr/0002-nature-dimension.md#contract-and-jurisdiction-2)

For a dataset with the coverage factor k, the kernel evaluates the model's prediction A exactly at each point, with the calibrated values. A point with the measured value v and the standard uncertainty u is consistent when (A − v)² ≤ k²·(u² + Σ_c (∂A/∂c)²·u_c²), summed over the calibrated coordinates c with their uncertainties u_c, with no square root. The verdict `consistent` holds exactly when every point is consistent. An accepted comparison records that verdict; another is an error (`E_ERRORBAR`), whose message names the first inconsistent point or states that every point is consistent.

- Example: At Ω = 5/2 the prediction at Δ is 25/(8Δ² + 50). The five points of the two-level program at Δ = 0, 1, 2, −1 and 5/2, with the values 1/2, 43/100, 3/10, 11/25 and 13/50 and the uncertainty 1/50, are consistent under k = 2, so the verdict `inconsistent` is an error (`E_ERRORBAR`). Moved to 3/5, the value at resonance is inconsistent, and the verdict `consistent` is the error.
- Run by: `each_mutation_of_an_expected_value_or_the_verdict_is_caught` in [`tests/two_level.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/two_level.rs)

Claims:

- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `each_mutation_of_an_expected_value_or_the_verdict_is_caught` in [`tests/two_level.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/two_level.rs)
    - `a_wrong_verdict_is_rejected` in [`tests/physical_models.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/physical_models.rs)
    - `book_rejected_packages_print_their_diagnostics` in [`tests/examples.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/examples.rs)
    - [`VastitasKernel.NatureModelRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasKernel/NatureModelRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)
- `oracle`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#841](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/841)
  - Note: The oracle theorem of the Stage 6 proof step: an accepted comparison's verdict is `consistent` exactly when every point satisfies the inequality of the statement, computed from the average and its exact derivative.
- `propagation`: [Not claimed](../specifications.md#not-claimed)
  - Reason: The inequality propagates the uncertainty of the calibration to first order and treats the uncertainties as uncorrelated. Both are assumptions of a comparison, which it states; no claim states that they hold for physical data, and an uncertainty never bounds the error of a numerical method.

<a id="physical-model.staleness"></a>

## A changed calibration makes its comparisons stale

- Property: `physical-model.staleness`
- Subject: `nature::errorbar::Comparison`
- Rule: [ADR 0002 §5, Contract and jurisdiction](../adr/0002-nature-dimension.md#contract-and-jurisdiction-2)

The fingerprint of a calibration is `fnv1a64:` and 16 hexadecimal digits: the FNV-1a digest of its canonical content, its calibrated coordinates in the order of the coordinates of the object with their values and uncertainties, its method, its reference and its revision. An accepted comparison records the current fingerprint of its calibration. Another fingerprint is an error (`E_STALE`) whose message names the current one, so that the comparison can be recorded again after a review.

- Example: The two-level program records `fnv1a64:fd1f7edd812db49f` for the calibration Ω = 5/2 ± 1/20. Evaluated again with the uncertainty 1/25, the calibration has another fingerprint, and the comparison is stale (`E_STALE`) until it records that one.
- Run by: `a_changed_calibration_is_stale_and_changes_no_std_code` in [`tests/two_level.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/two_level.rs)

Claims:

- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `a_changed_calibration_is_stale_and_changes_no_std_code` in [`tests/two_level.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/two_level.rs)
    - `a_changed_calibration_makes_the_comparison_stale` in [`tests/physical_models.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/physical_models.rs)
    - `forged_stage6_records_are_rejected_by_the_kernel` in [`tests/physical_models.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/physical_models.rs)
    - `book_rejected_packages_print_their_diagnostics` in [`tests/examples.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/examples.rs)

  - Note: The rejected package `two-level-stale` gives the diagnostic of the example. The forged wire records another fingerprint, which the kernel rejects with `E_STALE`.
- `oracle`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#841](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/841)
  - Note: The oracle theorem of the Stage 6 proof step: an accepted comparison's recorded fingerprint equals `calibrationFingerprint` of its calibration.

<a id="physical-model.limits"></a>

## Datasets and recorded texts are bounded

- Property: `physical-model.limits`
- Subject: `nature::errorbar::Dataset`
- Rule: [ADR 0002 §5, Execution and evidence profile](../adr/0002-nature-dimension.md#execution-and-evidence-profile-2)

A dataset has at most `datasetPoints` = 64 points; a larger one is an error (`E_LIMIT`) of the frontend at its list of points and of the kernel before it reads a point. A recorded text, the regime of a model, the reference and the revision of a calibration or the fingerprint of a comparison, holds at most `recordTextBytes` = 256 bytes of printable ASCII other than `\` and `"`. A longer literal is an error (`E_LIMIT`), and on the wire any other text is an error (`E_PROTOCOL`).

- Example: A dataset of 65 points is an error (`E_LIMIT`) and one of 64 points is accepted. A reference of 257 bytes is an error (`E_LIMIT`), and a forged regime with a backslash or 257 bytes is an error (`E_PROTOCOL`).
- Run by: `the_points_of_a_dataset_are_bounded` in [`tests/physical_models.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/physical_models.rs)

Claims:

- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `the_points_of_a_dataset_are_bounded` in [`tests/physical_models.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/physical_models.rs)
    - `stage6_syntax_errors_are_reported_at_their_place` in [`tests/physical_models.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/physical_models.rs)
    - `forged_stage6_records_are_rejected_by_the_kernel` in [`tests/physical_models.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/physical_models.rs)
    - [`VastitasKernel.ModelDeclarationRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasKernel/ModelDeclarationRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)

<a id="physical-model.weakening"></a>

## Models and data change no std code

- Property: `physical-model.weakening`
- Subject: `nature::model`
- Rule: [ADR 0002 §5, Laws](../adr/0002-nature-dimension.md#laws-2)

A convention, a model, a calibration, a dataset or a comparison changes no validity, no value and no generated code of a `std` declaration. Without them, and without the dependency on `nature`, the program generates the same code.

- Example: The two-level program without its comparison, and without every declaration of `nature`, generates byte-identical Lean and shows the same predictions.
- Run by: `a_changed_calibration_is_stale_and_changes_no_std_code` in [`tests/two_level.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/two_level.rs)

Claims:

- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `a_changed_calibration_is_stale_and_changes_no_std_code` in [`tests/two_level.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/two_level.rs)
    - `a_changed_calibration_makes_the_comparison_stale` in [`tests/physical_models.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/physical_models.rs)
- `oracle`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#841](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/841)
  - Note: The weakening theorems of the Stage 6 proof step, which extend those of `nature::dimension` to the declarations of `nature::model` and `nature::errorbar`: they change no std validity, value or generated code.

<a id="physical-model.regime"></a>

## The regime is recorded, not proved

- Property: `physical-model.regime`
- Subject: `nature::model::Model`
- Rule: [ADR 0002 §4, Contract and jurisdiction](../adr/0002-nature-dimension.md#contract-and-jurisdiction-1)

The regime of a model is a recorded assumption: a text that the kernel checks only for its characters and its length. No check reads its meaning, and an accepted model does not establish that the regime holds.

- Example: The two-level model records the regime "rotating-wave approximation, drive far below the transition frequency"; a model with another text is checked the same way.
- Not executed: the property states what no check establishes

Claims:

- `meaning`: [Not claimed](../specifications.md#not-claimed)
  - Reason: Whether a physical system is in the regime of its model, such as the rotating-wave approximation, is outside what an exact check of declarations can establish.
